metadata.description: DSH plugin: your DeepSeek account balance as a colour-banded bar on the right edge, with per-turn cost prediction and a quiet low-balance warning.
metadata.name: dsh-balance-guard

paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: your DeepSeek account balance as a colour-banded bar on the right edge, with per-turn co
st prediction and a quiet low-balance warning.
# dsh-balance-guard

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that pins your
**DeepSeek account balance** to the right edge of the GUI a

s a quiet colour-coded rail, and
**projects what the current task will cost** before the balance run

iet colour-coded rail, and
**projects what the current task will cost** before the balance runs out.

Nothing else changes hands: the balance comes from the DSH account you are already signed into,
the
API key is never read, and no message content leaves the Host.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Balance (account currency) | Band | Meaning |

| `< 10` | **red** | about to run dry |
| `10 – 30` | **orange** | top up soon |
| `30 – 50` | **gre

en** | fine |
| `> 50` | **blue** | plenty (the excess over the 50 mark is stated in the panel) |

Every colour, radius, shadow and type size comes from the shell's own `--dsw-*` tokens; there is
no

custom palette and no animation beyond a 160–240ms transition. Hover shows a read-only preview
of th
e panel, clicking pins it, `Esc` or a click outside closes it.
## 中文速览

- 界面最右缘一根 **4px 极简轨道**，按余额比例填充；旁边常驻一个 **20px 小胶囊**（语义色点 + 金额）。
- 颜色：`<10` 红、`10–30` 橙、`30–50` 绿、`>50

` 蓝；`>50` 的超出部分在面板里以「超刻度 ¥x」说明，
不再有波浪动画。
- 悬停 = 只读预览面板；点击 = 固定面板（`Esc` 或点击外部关闭）。面板里给出**本轮已花 / 预计还需区间

**；
预计不够跑完时胶囊上出现「!」徽标、面板里一行红字写缺口（不弹窗、不发声）。
- 余额来自已登录的 **DSH 账号**，不读 API Key；卡片可展开「估算依据」（步数、缓存命中、峰谷价）

。
- 全部视觉走 DSH 主题令牌：11/12/13/16 字号阶、R8/R12/R16 圆角、系统面板阴影；无自定义色板。
## What it predicts
「当前任务」= **the running turn of the current root session** (`turn/start` → `turn/end`).

- **Already spent** is provider truth: the four billed buckets of the turn
(`uncachedInputTokens`, `

cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `outputTokens`) read as a delta
against the cumulative `tokenU

sage` session projection, priced by the current model and period.
- **Still to come** is projected p

er step: the next prompt size comes from the provider-anchored
`contextPressure.projectedTokens`, ou

tput and prompt growth come from this turn's samples
(falling back to configured defaults), and the

cache-hit ratio is measured from the turn so far.
- **How many steps are left** is the mean steps-pe

r-turn of this session's completed turns
(default 8 when there is no history). The card reports a **

minimum / expected / maximum**:
one more step, the expected remaining steps, and twice the expected

steps with a 10-point-worse
cache hit and peak prices.
- **Verdict**: `required = expectedRemaining

× 1.2 + reserve`, compared against the balance minus
spend that landed *after* the balance reading (

Platform balance lags by minutes). Balance at or
below the line is "insufficient".

When no turn is running, the same card estimates the **next** task from the last three turns
instead
of pretending to know the future.
## Requirements

- A DSH client with the DeepSeek account signed in. The guard reads the balance through
`ctx.deepsee

kAccount`; the account token never reaches the renderer, and no API key is read.
- Node 20+ only for
the test/install scripts; the plugin itself has **no build step**.
## Where the number comes from

`ctx.deepseekAccount.getState()` and `getBalance()` — the same service the client's account menu
use

s, so the bar always agrees with what the client reports. **`getState()` is async**; reading it
sync

hronously once made every signed-in account look signed out, which is why the account section
of thi
s file points that out twice.

The card names the source (`余额来源：DSH 账号`). A reading that fails after a successful one stays
on scre

en, clearly labelled with the error; an explicit sign-out clears the figure and the bar turns
grey.
## Architecture
Two halves, one plugin.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Why a Host half?** The account token never reaches the renderer; per-turn billing lives in the
Hos

t's session log; and the `shell.overlay` entry does not receive `useProjection`, so the page
cannot
read session projections by itself.

**Why an HTTP route instead of `@Remote`?** Remote methods are generated from Host decorations by
th

e Typert build pipeline. A plugin outside the Harness build must describe its own wire protocol,
so

it publishes on `ctx.webServer` with an exact named route — deliberately *not* under `/api`,
which b

elongs to the Connection plugin and authenticates. Only aggregates cross the wire: no
tokens, no mes
sage text. The shipped Web composition binds loopback only.

**Why is every threshold on the Host?** So the product rules exist once (in `policy.js`), are
tested
once with plain Node, and a cached browser bundle can never disagree with the Host.
## Limitations

- **The projection is not a bill.** Remaining steps, cache-hit ratio and tool-output size are
estima

tes; the min/expected/max range is the honest error bar.
- **Platform balance lags** by tens of seco

nds to minutes. The guard subtracts measured spend that
landed after the reading, but that compensat

ion is itself measured.
- **Holidays are offline.** Without a `holidays` list, weekday peak windows

are priced as peak
(a conservative over-estimate).
- **Sub-agents are not in the projection.** Their

spend is real and shows up in the balance; the
card only notes that they are running.
- **One task

at a time.** With several sessions running, the Host tracks the most recently active
running turn; t

he card names the session title.
- **Prices may change.** The catalog carries a fetch date; a price

change is one constant plus one
test.
- **USD accounts** display in USD; the price catalog is conver

ted with `cnyPerUsd` only for CNY
accounts.
- **The account service must be composed.** The plugin d

eclares `deepseekAccount` and
`sessionProjections` as required services, so a profile without them l

oads no bar at all rather
than a broken one. Both ship with the Desktop client and `dsh web`.
- **Th

e in-app top-up page is not ours.** DSH's native Platform page belongs to the account
settings packa
ge, so the card's 去充值 opens the Platform top-up URL in the system browser.
